words.gloss: having the counsellor and the chaplain as companions

hindi: मन्त्री और पुरोहित सखा वाला सामान्य अधिकरणों में अमात्यों को स्थापित करके उपधाओं से शुद्ध करे।
english: With the counsellor and the chaplain as companions, [he] should, having placed the ministers in common offices, clear [them] by tests.
notes: Subject (the king) is not stated; '[he]' is supplied. upadhā is the technical term of the chapter; literally 'trick, test of honesty'; English 'test', Hindi उपधा kept. śodhayet/śuddha are kept literal ('clear'/शुद्ध), the sense 'examine' is not applied. adhikaraṇa = office (kept as adhikaraṇa in Hindi). sthāpayitvā 'placed' (alternative 'appointed'). 'mantri-' is the compound form of mantrin (no flag).

words.gloss: in officiating for the ayājya (one not to be sacrificed for) and in teaching

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. a-√mṛṣ

hindi: राजा अयाज्य के याजन और अध्यापन में नियुक्त, असहन करते हुए पुरोहित को नीचे गिराए।
english: The king should cast down the chaplain, appointed to the officiating for the ayājya (one not to be sacrificed for) and to teaching, not tolerating.
notes: ayājya kept untranslated (as yājya in 3.14); literally 'one not to be officiated for'. The compound ayājya-yājana-adhyāpane can also be read 'in officiating for and teaching the ayājya'; the Sanskrit has no ca inside the compound, so the plain reading is kept. amṛṣyamāṇam has no stated object ('it' not supplied). avakṣipet literally 'throw down'; usual sense 'disgrace/humiliate', not applied.

hindi: वह गुप्तचरों के द्वारा शपथपूर्वक एक-एक अमात्य को गुप्त रूप से उकसाए — “यह राजा अधार्मिक। अच्छा, उसके दूसरे धार्मिक को, उसके कुल के, निकाले गए राजकुमार, कुल्य, एक-प्रग्रह वाले, सामन्त, आटविक या औपपादिक को प्रस्तुत करते हैं। सभी को यह रुचता है, या तुम्हारा कैसा?”
english: He should, through secret agents, preceded by an oath, secretly instigate each single minister: “This king [is] unrighteous. Good, we put forward another righteous [one] of his: a member of his family, a prince in disfavour, a kinsman, one having a single grasp (eka-pragraha), a neighbouring chief, a forest chief or an aupapādika. This is pleasing to all; or how [is it] to you?”
notes: sattrin = secret agent (गुप्तचर) per glossary. Subject sa is the king (not named in the line). sādhu may instead be an adjective of anyam ('a good, righteous other'); it is rendered as an interjection as in unit 11. asya (genitive) is rendered 'his'; it may also mean 'in his place'. The list after anyam is taken as apposition (candidates), joined only by the final vā. eka-pragraha is obscure: rendered literally (pragraha 'grasp'; the glossary's 'favouring' is not applied), alternative readings in commentary not applied. pratipādayāmaḥ literally 'we cause to attain / hand over'; 'put forward' chosen, alternatives 'install', 'hand [the kingdom] over to'. aupapādika kept untranslated (glossary 5.2). The quote opened here closes with iti at the end of the unit, carried by the quotation marks. The mid-line dash introduces the quotation. kathaṃ vā tava is verbless: '[is it]' supplied in English only.

hindi: अस्वीकार पर शुचि। यह धर्म की उपधा है।
english: On refusal [he is] pure. Such is the test of dharma.
notes: Verbless: '[he is]' supplied in English only, the subject (the minister who refuses) is not stated. The '|' is the e-text's daṇḍa. Section label 'iti X' rendered 'Such is X' per glossary (iti glossed 'closing particle').

words.gloss: for the destruction of the king

hindi: सेनापति असत् के प्रग्रह से नीचे गिराया गया, गुप्तचरों के द्वारा एक-एक अमात्य को लुभाने वाले धन से राजा के विनाश के लिए गुप्त रूप से उकसाए — “सभी को यह रुचता है, या तुम्हारा कैसा?”
english: The commander of the army, cast down by favouring of the bad, should, through secret agents, secretly instigate each single minister by tempting wealth for the king's destruction: “This is pleasing to all; or how [is it] to you?”
notes: asat-pragraha follows the glossary (8.3) 'favouring of the bad'; here it may rather mean an improper favouring (of others) or improper treatment; sense low. The line has the commander as subject of upajāpayet; the king's part is not stated. lobhanīyena (gerundive 'to be coveted') is rendered 'tempting'. artha = wealth. The quote is short; the proposal itself is not repeated in the Sanskrit. iti closes the quotation (carried by the marks).

hindi: अस्वीकार पर शुचि। यह अर्थ की उपधा है।
english: On refusal [he is] pure. Such is the test of wealth.
notes: As unit 4. artha = wealth. Printed 'ity' is iti by sandhi (iti + a).

words.gloss: one who has had honour done
one who has made the means of meeting

hindi: परिव्राजिका, अन्तःपुर में विश्वास प्राप्त की हुई, सत्कार की हुई, एक-एक महामात्र को गुप्त रूप से उकसाए — “राजा की पटरानी तुम्हें चाहती है, मिलन का उपाय की हुई, और बड़ा धन तुम्हारा होगा।”
english: The parivrājikā (female wanderer), who has gained trust in the inner apartments, who has had honour done, should secretly instigate each single high official: “The king's chief queen desires you, having made the means of meeting; and great wealth will be yours.”
notes: parivrājikā is the feminine of parivrājaka (kept as a term, glossary 1.4). The two bahuvrīhi adjectives (labdha-viśvāsā, kṛta-satkārā) agree with her and have no ca between them, so no 'and'. antaḥpure is taken with labdha-viśvāsā ('trust in the inner apartments'). mahiṣī literally 'she-buffalo', the established sense 'chief queen' used. kṛta-samāgama-upāyā literally 'by whom the means of meeting is made'; samāgama may also mean union. iti closes the quotation (carried by the marks). The mid-line dash introduces the quotation.

hindi: अस्वीकार पर शुचि। यह काम की उपधा है।
english: On refusal [he is] pure. Such is the test of desire.
notes: As unit 4. kāma = desire.

words.gloss: for the purpose of a prahavaṇa

hindi: प्रहवण के निमित्त एक अमात्य सभी अमात्यों को बुलाए।
english: For the purpose of a prahavaṇa, one minister should summon all the ministers.
notes: prahavaṇa is obscure and kept untranslated (glossary 5.2/13.2); no sense is applied. āvāhayet literally 'cause to come'/'bring'; 'invite' is an alternative.

hindi: उस उद्वेग से राजा उन्हें रोक रखे।
english: By that agitation the king should confine them.
notes: tena agrees with udvegena ('that agitation'); udvega 'agitation, alarm', as udvigna (glossary 7.16). avarundhyāt literally 'obstruct, keep back'; 'confine' is the usual sense; Hindi keeps the literal 'रोक रखे'.

words.gloss: cast down in wealth and honour

hindi: और यहाँ पहले रोका गया कापटिक उनमें से अर्थ और मान में नीचे गिराए गए एक-एक अमात्य को गुप्त रूप से उकसाए — “यह राजा बुरी तरह प्रवृत्त। अच्छा, इसे मारकर दूसरे को प्रस्तुत करते हैं। सभी को यह रुचता है, या तुम्हारा कैसा?”
english: And here the kāpaṭika, previously confined, should secretly instigate each single minister of them cast down in wealth and honour: “This king [has] proceeded badly. Good, having killed him, we put forward another. This is pleasing to all; or how [is it] to you?”
notes: kāpaṭikaś = kāpaṭikaḥ before ca. kāpaṭika kept untranslated (glossary 5.2). pūrva-avaruddhaḥ teṣām may be read 'previously confined among them'; teṣām is taken with ekaikam amātyam (partitive). artha-māna-avakṣiptam: literally 'cast down in/by wealth and honour' (Kangle: slighted in respect of wealth and honour); case relation uncertain. 'asat pravṛttaḥ' is printed as two words; it could be a compound asat-pravṛtta ('engaged in the bad'); the adverbial reading is kept. sādhu as in unit 3. pratipādayāmaḥ as in unit 3. The quote closes with iti (carried by the marks).

hindi: अस्वीकार पर शुचि। यह भय की उपधा है।
english: On refusal [he is] pure. Such is the test of fear.
notes: As unit 4. bhaya = fear.

words.gloss: those cleared by the test of dharma
in the dharmasthīya (relating to the dharmasthas) and the cleansing of thorns
those cleared by the test of wealth
in the works of the Collector, the Treasurer and accumulation

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, f. (first part of compound kāma-upadhā-śuddhān)
m. acc. pl. (last member of compound kāma-upadhā-śuddhān)

words.gloss: in the protections of the outer and inner amusements
those cleared by the test of fear

hindi: वहाँ धर्म-उपधा से शुद्ध हुओं को धर्मस्थीय और कण्टकशोधन के कर्मों में स्थापित करे, अर्थ-उपधा से शुद्ध हुओं को समाहर्ता, सन्निधाता, निचय के कर्मों में, काम-उपधा से शुद्ध हुओं को बाहरी और भीतरी विहार की रक्षाओं में, भय-उपधा से शुद्ध हुओं को राजा के निकट के कार्यों में।
english: There [he] should place [those] cleared by the test of dharma in the works of the dharmasthīya (relating to the dharmasthas) and the cleansing of thorns; [those] cleared by the test of wealth, in the works of the Collector, the Treasurer and accumulation; [those] cleared by the test of desire, in the protection of the outer and inner amusements; [those] cleared by the test of fear, in the king's near tasks.

text_flags.why: stray space for a compound dot: the parallel members read dharma.upadhā.śuddhān, artha.upadhā.śuddhān, bhaya.upadhā.śuddhān (one compound)

notes: The verb sthāpayet governs all four clauses; in the later clauses it is left elliptical, as in the Sanskrit. '[he]' and '[those]' are supplied in English (participle śuddhān used as a noun); Hindi हुओं is the substantive use. Because of the stray space the compound kāma-upadhā-śuddhān is split over two tokens (first token 'kāma-upadhā', second 'śuddhān'). karma = works (glossary 5.1/5.3). dharma-sthīya: dharmastha kept as a title; kaṇṭaka-śodhana literally 'cleansing of thorns' (glossary 4.1), no later sense imported. samāhartṛ = the Collector, saṃnidhātṛ = the Treasurer (glossary 12.2/8.4); the printed 'samnidhātṛ' is the e-text's m spelling. nicaya literally 'heaping up, accumulation' (alternative 'store'); whether it names an office is uncertain. vihāra = amusement (glossary 8.4). āsanna-kārya literally 'near/proximate tasks'. tatra 'there' (alternative 'in that case').

words.gloss: those cleared by all the tests

hindi: सभी उपधाओं से शुद्ध हुओं को मन्त्री बनाए।
english: [He] should make [those] cleared by all the tests counsellors.
notes: Subject not stated: '[he]' supplied in English only. mantrin = counsellor (glossary 9.6); mantriṇaḥ is the accusative plural (second object of kuryāt). Hindi 'बनाए' for kuryāt (literally 'करे').

words.gloss: in the karmāntas of mines, produce forests and elephant forests

hindi: सर्वत्र अशुचियों को खान, द्रव्य-वन, हस्ति-वन के कर्मान्तों में लगाए।
english: [He] should employ [those] impure everywhere in the karmāntas of mines, produce forests and elephant forests.
notes: Subject and the noun with aśucīn are supplied in English ('[he]', '[those]'). sarvatra 'everywhere' (understood: in all the tests); kept literal. karma-anta is kept as the term karmānta (literally 'end of works'); the sense 'workshop, factory' is not applied. The compound is read with karmānta as head (dravya-vana, hasti-vana as in glossary 7.1/7.16); the alternative is a plain list 'mines, produce, elephants, forests, karmāntas'.

words.gloss: those thoroughly cleared by the triad and fear

hindi: त्रिवर्ग और भय से भली-भाँति शुद्ध हुए अमात्यों को अपने कर्मों में शुचिता के अनुसार अधिकृत करे, आचार्य निश्चित।
english: Ministers thoroughly cleared by the triad and fear, [he] should put in charge in their own works according to purity; the teachers [are] settled.
notes: trivarga = the triad (dharma, wealth, desire; glossary 1.7); the tests meant are the four upadhās, but the Sanskrit names only the triad and fear. 'iti' closes the statement with no opening quotation and is not rendered; ācāryā vyavasthitāḥ = ācāryāḥ vyavasthitāḥ. vyavasthita literally 'settled, fixed'; Kangle takes it as 'the settled view of the teachers'. The English copula for the verbless last clause is bracketed; Hindi has none. adhi-√kṛ literally 'set over'. karma = works.

hindi: किन्तु स्वामी अपने को या देवी को लक्ष्य न ही बनाए। अमात्यों की शुचिता के कारण यह कौटिल्य का मत।
english: But the lord should not indeed make himself or the queen a target. On account of the purity of the ministers, this [is] Kautilya's view.
notes: īśvara 'lord' (the king; Hindi स्वामी to avoid 'God'). devī = queen (glossary 7.15). lakṣyam literally 'mark, target' (of the tests/agents). amātyānām is taken with śauca-hetoḥ ('purity of the ministers'). darśana 'view'. The English copula for the last clause is bracketed, none in Hindi.

hindi: अदुष्ट का दूषण आचरण न करे, जैसे विष से जल का। क्योंकि पूरी तरह दूषित का औषध कभी न मिले।
english: [One] should not practise the defiling of the undefiled, like [the defiling] of water by poison. For a remedy of the thoroughly corrupted would not ever be found.
notes: Subject of caret not stated: '[one]' in English only. 'viṣeṇa iva ambhasaḥ' repeats dūṣaṇam ('like [the defiling] of water by poison'), bracketed in English only; Hindi leaves it elliptical. kadācid hi: the e-text's 'dd h' for d+dh/t+h is its habit (w reads kadācit). kadācit … na = 'not ever'. bheṣaja kept as plain 'remedy' (Hindi औषध). aduṣṭasya/praduṣṭasya are genitives of a person or thing; no noun supplied.

hindi: और उपधाओं से कलुषित की गई, चार प्रकार की, बुद्धि, सत्त्ववानों की धृति में स्थित, अन्त को पहुँचे बिना न लौटे।
english: And the mind made stained by the tests, fourfold, established in the steadiness of the spirited, would not turn back without having gone to the end.

text_flags.why: possible stray compound dot: kaluṣā is a feminine adjective agreeing with buddhiḥ (a compound would have kaluṣa-buddhi); the words are read as two

notes: Subject of nivarteta is buddhiḥ, with kṛtā, kaluṣā, caturvidhā and sthitā agreeing. na-agatvā: na negates nivarteta, agatvā = 'without having gone' (a-gatvā), so the sense is 'would not turn back without reaching the end'. kaluṣā kṛtā taken as 'made stained' (alternative: 'made, stained'). caturvidhā 'fourfold' agrees with buddhiḥ and alludes to the four upadhās. sattvavat 'possessing spirit' (sattva = spirit, glossary 5.6). ca 'and' joins the unit to what precedes.

hindi: इसलिए चार प्रकार के कार्य में बाहरी आधार बनाकर राजा गुप्तचरों के द्वारा अमात्यों की शुचिता और अशुचिता को खोजे।
english: Therefore, having made an outer basis in the fourfold task, the king should seek out the purity and impurity of the ministers through secret agents.
notes: adhiṣṭhāna literally 'standing-place, basis' (commentators: a pretext, not applied). bāhya 'outer'. The fourfold task = the four upadhās of the chapter. mārg = seek out (glossary 4.7). sattrin = secret agent.
